body_long:
Mandarin Oriental has topped the LTI ranking of the world's best luxury hotel brands for the fourth year running, with a score of 81.1%. The 2026 results come from Luxury Travel Intelligence, which released them on 27 October, and were reported by Journal du Luxe on 6 November.

## How the ranking works

LTI audits 20 brands this year, up from 15. Each is assessed on 134 touchpoints, weighted towards a maximum of 4,792 points and then expressed as a percentage. The criteria judge the performance of the company as a whole rather than its hotels one by one, and a brand needs at least eight properties to qualify. The evaluation starts from scratch each year, so last year's result carries no weight.

## The top ten

1. Mandarin Oriental, 81.1% (1st last year)
2. Oetker Collection, 80.6% (4th)
3. Bulgari, 80.2% (3rd)
4. Four Seasons, 78.7% (6th)
5. Rosewood, 78.0% (5th)
6. Dorchester Collection, 76.9% (12th)
7. Belmond, 76.6% (11th)
8. Capella, 76.1% (new entry)
9. Aman, 75.5% (2nd)
10. Airelles, 75.2% (new entry)

Dorchester Collection is the biggest climber, up six places. Oetker Collection gains two. Capella and Airelles enter the ranking directly in the top ten. Aman drops from second to ninth; Journal du Luxe sets the fall against the cyberattack the group suffered in April. Further down, COMO, Jumeirah and Ritz-Carlton are also new entries, at 17th, 18th and 19th.

## Mandarin Oriental's year

The title comes in the group's first year as a private company, after it was taken private in January 2026 at a valuation of 4.2 billion dollars, according to Journal du Luxe. Laurent Kleitman, the group's chief executive, has set the aim of doubling the portfolio to 100 hotels in the coming years. Journal du Luxe also reports a 10% rise in RevPAR in 2025.

## The signal

This ranking rewards consistency across a whole portfolio, not the shine of one flagship. That favours collections that grow slowly and control every address. Oetker Collection and Dorchester Collection, whose hotels between them span Paris, London and the Riviera, now both sit in the top six. For Mandarin Oriental, the test ahead is whether that consistency holds as the portfolio doubles.

Congratulations to the teams of Mandarin Oriental and of every brand in this year's top ten.
summary: Mandarin Oriental leads with 81.1%, ahead of Oetker Collection and Bulgari. Dorchester Collection climbs from 12th to 6th, Aman falls from 2nd to 9th.
